correctness.rationale: Derived smooth return F_c(y)=sqrt((sqrt(y)-y)/c)-(sqrt(y)-y) on invariant positive (0,1) since c>4/25. Unique Nash has y*=1/(1+c)^2; F_c prime at Nash equals -(1-c)^2/(4c). For a putative u<v two-cycle, alternating best-response square equations imply 2cS²-(1+c)S+1=0 with S=a+b+u+v<2/(1+c); discriminant c²-6c+1 excludes primitive cycles when c>=3-2sqrt2. Applying Coppel no-two-cycle theorem to the continuous compact extension yields convergence to a fixed point; F(y)~c^-1/2 y^1/4 rules out zero from positive starts. Below threshold G=F²-y has sign changes around the repelling Nash point and positive near zero, giving cycle; quadratic root plus squared difference recovers unique unordered cycle. Independent numerical iterations and exact source witness at c=1/6 corroborate the transition; universality rests on the algebra and interval theorem.
